messages:
maria: heads up — saw a reproducible p99 spike (~2.8s -> 4.6s) when the autoscaler added nodes during the 11:10 burst. flame + perf logs attached in the ticket.

aj: can you paste the kernel selector trace? wondering if it fell back to the slower quant path during scaleup.

maria: sure — here's the snippet from the runtime log around the spike:

```
[KERNEL_SELECTOR] seq_len=1024, batch=3 -> prefer=fast-fp16, chosen=quantized-slow, reason=cache_miss_kv, latency_est=82ms->420ms
[KV_CACHE] miss for model=redwood-7b-v1 shard=3, cold=true
[PROBER] last_probe=22s ago, sample_count=6, fallback_threshold=0.25
```

sasha: aha — looks like two things: (1) KV cache misses on the new node are forcing a path that hits quantized kernels, (2) our prober sample_size is tiny so it underestimates the fast-fp16 viability on that node.

ken: +1. Also note microbatch sizing: when batch=3 we cross a heuristic boundary and the kernel selector prefers different tiling which multiplies latency. That combined with KV miss explains the tail.

aj: proposed short-term mitigations:
- increase prober sample_count -> 30 for 90s after node join
- extend prewarm window to 120s (prefill KV for hot model shards)
- adjust microbatch cap: cap at 2 for ramps during autoscale to avoid hitting the kernel boundary until KV warm

maria: can we do a canary of those 3 together? which one has the least runtime risk?

sasha: I'd start with prober tuning + sample_count. Lowest blast radius: just more probes, no kernel or batching code change. Prewarm is next (needs K8s job change). Microbatch cap is highest risk (affects throughput math).

ken: quick perf numbers from a local sim (cold KV):
- baseline: p95=1.2s, p99=2.8s
- cold new node + batch=3: p95=1.6s, p99=4.6s
- with prober=30 & prewarm 120s (simulated prefill): p95=1.25s, p99=2.9s

maria: nice — that suggests prober + prewarm recovers most tail. I'll open a short-run experiment ticket and schedule a canary tomorrow 9:00 UTC.

aj: for the canary, let's also capture per-token and kernel breakdown in the trace exporter so we can see which kernel is chosen after each probe. add metric: runtime.kernel_choice{node,model,seq_len,batch}.

deploy-bot: deploy request created: canary/prober-prewarm-191700 — will run on 4% traffic in us-west1.

maria: after canary, if stable, roll prober sample_count->30 globally and enable prewarm for tier=prod-hot models only. keep microbatch cap on hold.

ken: follow-up item: add a small warmup job that streams a few short requests to new nodes as they come up (cheap KV prefill). I can prototype.

sasha: add a dashboard panel for node-join tail spikes and kernel_choice heatmap. want to catch regressions earlier.

aj: ack. I'll own the canary instrumentation. maria — assign the ticket to me + ken.

maria: assigned. thanks all :thumbsup:
